To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the superconducting critical temperature Tc of the monolayer of FeSe grown on the SrTiO3 substrate can be explained in the framework of the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity, taking into account the influence of antiadiadatic phonons and the Coulomb pseudopotentil.

the superconducting critical temperature is determined by the partial contributions of adiabatic (low-frequency) phonons only, and that the Coulomb pseudopotenial is independent of the antiadiabatic (high-frequency) phonons.
the antiadiabatic optical phonons do not influence the value of the Coulomb pseudpotential, which is the only factor, that limits the superconducting critical temperature in the Eliashberg theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of antiadiadatic phonons on superconductivity.
the problem of an influence of antiadiadabatic phonons onto the superconducting properties of the materials, which are described by the Eliashberg theory of superconductivity.
the influence of antiadiadatic phonons on superconductivity within Eliashberg approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the superconducting state in monolayer FeSe on STO is not an exotic superconductor, but rather the superconductivity in monolayer of FeSe on STOs is the same as the superconductivity of bulk FeSe.
the antiadiabatic nature of phonons in FeSe monolayers is a key feature of the superconducting state, which is responsible for the high Tc values.
antiadiabatization is not a necessary condition for high Tc in FeSe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antiadiabatic optical phonons are not responsible for the high Tc of FeSe monolayers on STO.
antiadiabatical phonons do not affect superconductivity in the framework of Eliashberg-McMillan theory.
antiadiabatical effects are not important for the superconducting properties of FeSe monolayers on STO.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Coulomb pseudopotenial m* can be very small, even if the electron-phonon coupling is strong.

the contribution of antiadiabatical phonons is negligible and that the high superconducting temperature in the FeSe/STO system can be explained by strong electron-phonon coupling and a large density of states at the Fermi level.
the contribution of antiadiabatically coupled phonons into the superconducting Tc is small, and the value of the Coulomb pseudopotenial m* is determined by adiabatically coupled phonon modes only.
